FAQ

What is RNGdle?

RNGdle is a daily random number game inspired by the thrill of one clean roll. Each day, the player generates a number from 0 to 1,000,000 and the game scans it for patterns such as primes, palindromes, repeated digits, lucky sevens, clean endings, and special number references.

The fun comes from turning pure randomness into a scorecard. A plain number can still earn common badges, while rare coincidences such as exact special numbers, long repeated runs, or unusual mathematical properties can produce huge EP swings.

How does scoring work?

Every matched badge has an EP value. Common badges such as Even, Odd, Pair, or Six Digits add small amounts, while rare badges such as Jackpot, Leet, Exact Nice, or six repeated sevens are worth dramatically more.

Some badges belong to the same family. In those cases, only the strongest badge in that family contributes EP, while the rest still appear as supporting discoveries. This keeps one lucky pattern from double-counting too aggressively.

Is this version daily?

Yes. This static version stores one roll per UTC day in the browser using localStorage. The next roll becomes available after the UTC midnight countdown reaches zero.

Accounts are available for signing in across visits, while roll history, lifetime EP, and the daily lock still live on the current device.

What is different from the live RNGdle site?

The core gameplay loop is reproduced: generate a daily number, reveal badges, calculate EP, estimate rarity, and share the result.

This version includes authenticated profiles, but global leaderboards, hearts, friend feeds, and server-issued claim tokens are still represented as local-only behavior here.
